Countries worldwide are seeing massive drops in workforce participation, many of those listed countries have even lower rates than the US. This isn't a matter of [insert color] people. It's a matter of worker productivity skyrocketing. In the 50s if it took 50 people to provide the goods and services for 100 people, those same 50 people can now provide the goods and services for 600 people. Really - worker productivity, cross sector, is up 600! When you need 1/6th as many people to maintain production labor participation rates decline because the jobs aren't there. You also see other consequential issues as we have in the US including stagnant wages and a gradual decline in economic growth: less people working = less people getting paid = less money to go back into companies.

If you're still dead set on blaming immigrants, then this ought be eye opening. The US has a rather low net migration rate and it's been declining as our country continues to deteriorate. Many of the countries listed above have substantially greater migration rates per population.
